clue.text: Note attached to item of furniture for restorer

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a dresser is a kitchen cabinet with shelves

explanation.surface: A musical note pinned to a piece of furniture for the person repairing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts right a wrong or a fault, setting things back as they were, redresses it.

clue.text: Superior installed in tiptop accommodation, which is right in theory

indicators.note: something installed in a place is set inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I
a prior is the superior of a religious house

explanation.surface: A monastic head lodged in first-class rooms, which is only proper in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (tiptop) is taken as A and I, with PRIOR placed between them; 'accommodation, which is right' is surface padding linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning from theory rather than observed experience is the Latin-phrase sense used by philosophers.

clue.text: Extends car-port maybe on back street

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of the word car-port could be arranged another way
back asks for the abbreviation for street to be read from right to left

explanation.surface: A garage roof attached to the rear of a road is lengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns CARPORT into PROTRACT; 'back' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag out or lengthen something in time is a synonym of extending it.

clue.text: A painter does-given a list

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them, so does gives cons
a table is a list of figures or facts set out in rows

explanation.surface: An artist cheats when handed a roster.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable is the famous English landscape artist, an example of a painter.

clue.text: Swear about Opposition leader's procedure

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to swear is to curse

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone uses bad language about the head of the Opposition's methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of action is a way of proceeding, a method.

clue.text: A point the commanding officer pressed, being beaten

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: A military commander insisted on a particular point.
explanation.definitionFit: Scourged means whipped or flogged, a past participle matching beaten.

clue.text: Cooked sausage — still

indicators.note: cooked suggests the word sausage is prepared and changed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A sausage that has been cooked lies motionless on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To still pain or fear is to calm or soothe it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: The rest of one's days

parts.note: reads as the remainder of a lifetime, but means the rest or free time within each day

explanation.surface: The remainder of a person's life.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time for relaxation is the rest part of any day, not the end of a life.

clue.text: Ways some love, providing material for the paper

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are compass directions or ways
some of a thing is a part of it
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Different routes for a little affection, supplying copy for the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Esparto is a tough grass of Spain and North Africa used in making fine paper.
explanation.definitionFit: This coarse Mediterranean grass is a raw fibre used in papermaking.

clue.text: Overcomes with' a 'certain audacity — such a bloomer

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate and subdue them
lip is cheeky talk or impudence

explanation.surface: Someone wins through with a certain cheek, an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered meadow plant is a flower, a bloomer.

clue.text: Roll round about one and create a disturbance

indicators.note: round about means encircling, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tumble about and make a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily and boisterously, making a commotion.

clue.text: Fight, as cut out to be a rebel leader

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of as cut are put out of order

explanation.surface: Battling, as one is made for it, to become a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AS CUT to TACUS. Spartacus led the slave revolt against Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator headed the great slave uprising against Rome.

clue.text: Attending to get something for nothing

explanation.surface: Being there to receive a free gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Present means in attendance, and also a gift, which costs the recipient nothing.

clue.text: An individual running out of personal cover

definitions.text: An individual running out of personal cover

parts.words: An individual running out of personal cover
parts.note: suggests a sportsman leaving shelter, but describes someone dashing about without clothes

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying from a protective position.
explanation.definitionFit: A naked runner who dashes across a sports field or public place sheds all clothing.

clue.text: The number of the Spanish flat

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
flat ground is level or even

explanation.surface: The figure for a Spanish apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal figure, one more than ten, is a number.

clue.text: There's fish and fruit only

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit
sole means only, single

explanation.surface: A menu offering just seafood and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish of European waters, popular on menus.

clue.text: … fruit used to make a delicious drink in the Orient

parts.note: nectar is the drink of the gods
E, east, is the Orient

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, fruit pressed into a lovely drink in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is a fruit.

clue.text: Changing diet say in a Scottish region

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of diet say are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Advice on altering one's eating habits in part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Tayside was a local government region of Scotland, around Dundee and the River Tay.
explanation.definitionFit: The former administrative area round Dundee was one of Scotland's regions.

clue.text: Never to name it would be wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters of to name it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice that naming something should never happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning on no occasion, an adverb like never.

clue.text: Finding others without is to check

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece is put around the other

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Discovering that other people lack it serves as a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: REST wraps IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to hold back or stop something, which is what check means here.

clue.text: When climbing fell over an explosive device — investigate

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to fell a tree is to axe it
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: While scaling a peak someone tripped over a bomb and must look into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a hill or a tumble but is the verb to chop down; 'When climbing' turns AXE to EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect it closely, a synonym.

clue.text: Put in office with pomp and ceremony

definitions.meaning: to establish someone in a post

explanation.surface: Appointed to a post amid great formality.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone in a post is this verb, and read as two words it means in grand style.

clue.text: Minimal wear single folk have cut again!

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so one piece is set within the other

parts.note: bis means twice or again, an encore call
I, one, is single
kin are one's folk, relatives

explanation.surface: Unmarried people have cut skimpy clothing even smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS is a musical direction meaning repeat; I and KIN go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-piece swimsuits are skimpy beach clothing, so minimal garments.

clue.text: The person who's relatively biased

parts.note: relatively means somewhat, but here means in favour of relatives

explanation.surface: Someone who is fairly prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: One who favours family members in giving jobs or posts is partial to kin.

clue.text: Property of some interest -a tentative offer seems likely

indicators.note: some means just a part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A house of some appeal; a cautious bid looks likely.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions owned, property.

clue.text: A step taken by game fellows to acquire travel documents

parts.note: pas is a dance step, from French
good sports are game, willing fellows

explanation.surface: Willing players take a step to get their papers for going abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Official papers allowing travel abroad are the documents named.

clue.text: Set-back followed by row makes more cantankerous

indicators.note: back tells us the word set is read from right to left

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A setback followed by an argument makes someone grumpier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats; 'back' turns SET to TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Large attic in dreadful mess

indicators.note: a dreadful mess is disorder, so the letters of attic in are scrambled

explanation.surface: A big loft in a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, huge, from the Titans of myth.

clue.text: Sizeable hotel built with European capital

parts.note: tall means of great height, sizeable
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A large hotel erected with European money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but means a capital city: Tallinn, capital of Estonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn is the capital of Estonia, a European capital city.

clue.text: Guard around royalty showing great respect

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a guard is a defence
R and E, Rex or Regina plus Elizabeth, the royal cipher letters

explanation.surface: A protective shield around the royal family shows high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Deference is courteous regard and submission, high esteem shown to another.
